fix.cause:
The Kaiser fits two body plans at once, and the written rules give no way to pick one. Its four legs fit spider-frame, which is a body hung on several visible legs. Its gun layout fits casemate, which is a main gun fixed facing forward with no main turret.

Coder A followed the term rules. Casemate's class, mobility and size lists leave out walkers, many legs and huge size, and the vocabularies intro calls a left-out class a hard ban. So A kept the one term that breaks nothing, followed the checked RA3 Sickle (four legs, no main turret, coded spider-frame) and added a fit_note for the fixed gun.

Coder B read the casemate or hull-turret tie-break as a general test: decide by where the main gun sits, and a gun fixed in the hull gives casemate. B then treated casemate's class, mobility and size lists as rules a real unit may break. The vocabularies intro and the validator allow that for real units, so B recorded the three ATYPICAL lines.

Three gaps let both careful readings stand:
1. The only tie-break about where the gun sits names casemate and hull-turret. Nothing ranks spider-frame against any hull body.
2. The list description makes the body plan the upper-body shape and leaves legs to mobility, yet spider-frame is defined by its legs.
3. Nothing says whether a source unit may take a body its class list bans when an allowed body also fits. R1 has one case each way: the Sickle sits inside its lists, and the Mecha Tengu (a humanoid robot that hovers) sits outside them because no hover body has its shape.

A fourth reading, multi-turret, is also left open, because the Kaiser's wiki page calls its four ball-mounted machine guns turrets. Both coders set it aside.
fix.rule_now:
data/vocab/bodies.json, shown in docs/vocabularies.md under Body plans:

1. **casemate ('Fixed-gun hull'):** a main gun fixed facing forward and no main turret. Its classes are only vehicle and hover, its mobility only wheels, tracks and hover, and its sizes only medium and large.
2. **spider-frame:** a body hung between several visible legs, up 'to a giant walker'. It takes walker or drone on many legs only, with no size or mount limit.
3. **tie_breaks, third entry (casemate or hull-turret):** decide by 'where the main gun sits'. A gun fixed in the hull gives casemate; a gun in a turret gives hull-turret. No entry sets spider-frame against a hull body.
4. **The list description:** a body plan is the 'upper-body shape and silhouette', and legs 'live in mobility'.
5. **docs/vocabularies.md, the opening Rules bullet (written by scripts/build-docs.mjs):** a class left out is 'a hard ban'. The schemas/vocabulary.schema.json text for terms[].classes says the same. But the same bullet says real units that break a rule are 'recorded as they are' and listed as atypical.

A used points 1, 2 and the hard-ban line, plus the Sickle in data/units/ra3.json. B used point 3 and the 'recorded as they are' line, as the Mecha Tengu's entry did.

R4 will meet this shape often. By their usual descriptions, StarCraft II's Protoss walkers (the Stalker, the Immortal, the Colossus, and co-op walkers such as the Dragoon) and Halo Wars' Locust and Scarab stand on several legs with the main weapon set in the body, not in a turret that turns. fix.meanwhile:
Code by the current rules, read this way: a walker on many legs whose main gun is fixed, or sits in mounts that do not turn all the way round, is spider-frame. That is the only term whose rules take the walker class, many legs and any size without a break. Casemate's own lists leave out walkers and many legs (and huge size, for the Kaiser), the casemate or hull-turret tie-break only chooses between those two terms, and the checked Sickle is the precedent.

For each such unit:
- Record the fixed gun as the main weapon's body-aim mount.
- Describe the hull and the locked gun housing in body.notes.
- Record no bodies atypical.
- Add an uncertain entry at body/plan. Its note: casemate is the other reading, since the main gun is fixed in the body; it is set aside because casemate's lists leave out walkers and many legs; and the choice is an R3 rule problem for the round after R4.
- Keep one fit_note at body/plan in A's wording (wanted: a fixed-gun hull on legs), because the current rules send every gap there and the gap report reads only the files. The round removes it if option A is approved.

What this means for the units:
- **Kaiser, reconciled entry:** spider-frame, plus A's body.notes, the uncertain entry and A's fit_note; drop B's three bodies:casemate atypicals.
- **Mocny, in the fill:** the same pattern, with its cannon body-aim.
- **Stark, Grimbart and Nakovalnya:** coded as usual (spider-frame, an arm-gun body, launcher-rack). Each needs the uncertain entry only if its coder doubts the body plan.

So the fill jobs see this, add one line to the Iron Harvest research notes in research/registry-notes/games-r3.md, in the style of the existing Mech Hunter note. Add the same line to the R4 notes when they are written.

problems: Option A's rule contradicts itself (the proposed fourth tie-break in data/vocab/bodies.json). Its first sentence makes any walker on many legs with two or more fully turning turrets multi-turret. That clause has no condition on the main gun and no order against hull-turret. Its third sentence then says a main gun fixed facing forward keeps a walker spider-frame. So a walker with a fixed main gun and two such turrets for its other guns gets two answers. As multi-turret it would also break multi-turret's mount list, and its size and tier lists when it is not huge and t3. The analyst's own notes had 'huge, t3' in that clause; the final text dropped it. A walker whose main gun sits in one of two full turrets matches both hull-turret and multi-turret. The clause also goes against the existing casemate or hull-turret tie-break, which decides by the main gun even when a small turret carries another gun (the Magrider).

The interim ('meanwhile') line looks only at the main gun, so under A's wording the interim answer and the final answer differ for that same case: spider-frame now, multi-turret after the round. The blocks_r4 claim that units coded the interim way 'need no new body plan after the round' therefore fails for the very R4 unit the analyst names as a multi-turret risk, the Halo Wars Scarab.

A reaches well past the split. It covers every walker on many legs except launcher racks and creatures, and decides each by turret mechanics. Iron Harvest's Zolw becomes hull-turret: its cached wiki page shows a four-legged bunker that carries a squad, with a roof mortar turret that turns all the way round. That clashes with the troop-carrier tie-break, and A's own 'against' text says the Zolw case stays unwritten. Brunhilde (a main gun on top with a full field of fire, on four legs) and the Isegrim (a turning turret on four crab legs) would also be settled as hull-turret. None of these is coded or kept, so nothing needs recoding. But the rule gets ahead of R4's evidence: a spider-shaped walker whose head a source calls a turret (perhaps the Colossus) would be forced to hull-turret, against the list's 'shape and silhouette' definition.

A smaller fix does the same job. One tie-break can cover only a walker on many legs whose main weapon is fixed or does not turn all the way round: it is spider-frame, whatever its other weapons. Locked housings count as fixed, and ball mounts and side guns do not turn all the way. The casemate or hull-turret tie-break is limited to vehicles and hovercraft. Both Kaiser codings get the same single answer, R1 and R3 come out the same, the interim reading becomes the rule itself, and no turret order is needed. Tested in a scratch clone that keeps its .git: validate OK, docs build OK, 297 of 297 tests pass. The analyst's 296 of 297 came from a copy without .git. Both Kaiser files, recoded to spider-frame, validate with only the legs-multi atypical.

The meanwhile line drops A's exceptions for launcher racks and creatures. Written word for word into the R4 notes, it reads as making every many-legged walker with a fixed main weapon spider-frame. That would catch StarCraft II's many-legged Zerg creatures coded as walkers, and walker launcher racks. It has to carry the exceptions, plus 'whatever its other weapons'.

In the meanwhile section, 'an arm-gun body' for the Grimbart is not a body term. Its cached wiki page shows a box on stubby legs, with no leg count and two arms, the gatling on one of them. So it is humanoid-mech on two legs and spider-frame on many.

The under_fix part for coder B lists the plan, the three bodies:casemate atypicals and the fit_note. It misses that B's body.notes also says the body tie-break makes the Kaiser a fixed-gun hull and points to fit_notes. That sentence has to be rewritten as well; the reconciled entry avoids the problem by taking A's body.notes.

The recodes list miscounts: it says 'the four Generals', but research/r3/prep/trim.json keeps nine Generals units and nine Tempest Rising units. The claim itself holds: none of them walks on many legs. The Tempest Rising Sentinel, for example, is a wheeled scout car on its cached wiki page.

The R4 reasoning has gaps. MechWarrior is not wholly outside this case: its registry entry in data/games.json reads the BattleTechWiki's tabletop Technical Readouts, which include four-legged 'Mechs whose weapons fire forward, so one kept in R4 would be exactly this case. PA TITANS is never mentioned. Its unit database gives every weapon how far it turns (the Atlas's weapon turns 360 degrees), so a legged titan with a fully turning main weapon would fall outside this split.
verdict.blocks_r4: No. R4 can code these walkers by the current rules plus the interim line, each with an uncertain entry and a fit_note. Nothing reads body plans before the round, because plan step 4 comes after it. With the narrowed rule below, the interim line and the fix are the same sentence, so the round only removes uncertain entries and fit_notes; under option C the move would still be mechanical. Three corrections to the analyst's reasons. (1) Under the analyst's wording the interim answer and the fix differ for a walker with a fixed main gun and two or more fully turning turrets: multi-turret against spider-frame. That is the Halo Wars Scarab case the analyst raises, so 'no new body plan after the round' did not hold. (2) The R4 line must carry the launcher-rack, troop-carrier and creature exceptions. Without them it reads as covering StarCraft II's many-legged Zerg creatures and walker launcher racks. (3) MechWarrior is not wholly outside: the registry reads the tabletop readouts, whose four-legged 'Mechs would be this case. Walkers whose main weapon turns all the way round fall outside this split, for example the Colossus if a source says its head turns, or a legged PA titan, since PA's database gives each weapon's turn. They are coded by the current rules and go to the same round if they split.

fix.cause:
Both coders read CNCNZ's GLA units page. It gives Kell's Sniper Attack an instant cooldown. The wiki infobox and the unedited 1.04 Weapon.ini both give a reload of about half a minute, which is the medium band. Both coders logged that clash in an uncertain entry with sources_disagree. Where they differ is the fifth source slot.

A gave the fifth slot to CNCNZ. A followed the sources rule, which prefers another established site to a third page of one site, and the games-r1 note, which makes CNCNZ (kind guide) that other site. With CNCNZ cited, A applied the High or Medium tie-break: the clash decides a band, no official text settles it, and game data does not count as official text. So A coded medium.

B gave the slot to Weapon.ini, a third page of TheSuperHackers' repository. The slot order puts first the pages that give a figure the entry uses, and Weapon.ini holds the reload. B left CNCNZ uncited and named it only in an uncertain entry. B then took the sources rule at its word: confidence counts only cited pages, and a guide must be cited to count. The cited pages agree, so B coded high.

The written rules allow both codings because:
- the level is worked out from the cited pages, while the fifth slot is a free choice here;
- the tie-break does not say whether it reads uncited pages;
- no rule says whether a guide is an established site.

So the same pages read can give either level. On which pages count, the checked R1 data reads it A's way: ra1.allied.field-mechanic is medium because of a clash with the rules copy, which is named in an uncertain entry but not cited. No R1 case shows whether a guide's clash counts.
fix.rule_now:
- schemas/source-unit.schema.json, $defs.unit.properties.sources.description (shown in docs/fields.md, Source unit section, sources[] row). Confidence "counts only the cited pages", and an uncited guide "must be cited to count". The five slots go to the official page first, then to the pages most of the entry rests on, with "another established site" preferred to "a third page" of one site.
- data/vocab/confidence.json, tie_breaks[0].rule (docs/vocabularies.md, Confidence levels). When "established sites" clash on a point that decides a coded term (a band, for example) and "no official text settles it", the entry drops to medium.
